title: Instruction — block tree, version 1
description: Validates the BLOCK TREE a parser produces from an instruction, not the Markdown itself. Pipeline: parse Markdown with the grammar in x-grammar → emit this JSON shape → validate → apply the semantic rules in x-semantic-rules, which JSON Schema cannot express. Every kind's disposition, family, grant, forms, body type and acknowledgement template are carried as x- keywords so a validator in any language can be driven entirely from this file.

frontMatter.$comment: Unknown keys are preserved and ignored (§3.1 rule 2).

lang.$comment: code bodies: the fence info string

rows.$comment: table bodies, parsed: one object per row, keyed by header

sigil.$comment: true iff written with the ! sigil

children.$comment: blocks nested inside this one, sub-blocks included

members.$comment: set form only: one block per row / entry, form = member

mcp.x-acknowledgement: [mcp server "{name}" is connected; its tools are available]

x-semantic-rules.rule: For every kind with x-identity, attrs.name is unique across all top-level blocks and set members of that kind in the document. Sub-block names are scoped to their parent.
A bare (sigil=false) block whose kind is in x-registry.machinery is refused: 'did you mean :::!kind'. Applies to container, leaf and set forms; never to headings or keywords.
A sigiled block whose kind is in x-registry.prose or x-registry.structural is refused: 'did you mean :::kind'.
A sigiled block whose kind is not in x-registry.machinery is refused, naming the implemented version and the known set. (An unknown BARE kind never reaches the tree: the parser emits it as prose.)

Every @kind/name in attrs, every quoted @kind/name in a YAML body, every [[kind/name]] and [text](#kind/name) in prose resolves to a top-level block or set member of that kind with that name; otherwise refuse.
The graph of local references is acyclic; a cycle is refused naming the cycle. Cross-document references are cycle-guarded at resolution with published depth and fan-out caps.
A block whose kind has x-parent appears only in the children of a block of that parent kind. (The schema enforces the child side; a parser must not emit a sub-block at the top level.)
A leaf-form block of a kind whose x-body is not 'none' is refused unless the kind lists 'leaf' in x-forms.
A section-form block of a kind whose x-body is yaml/code contains exactly one fenced code block, which is the definition; surrounding prose becomes attrs.description.
A set body is entirely a table or entirely a definition list; the parser refuses otherwise. A kind whose x-body is deflist does not take the set form.
Fences, leaves and section headings are recognized at column 0 only; indented ones are prose.
Inside a fenced code block, no fence, leaf, keyword, alert or inline form is recognized. Inline forms are also inert inside inline code.
Keyword lines are recognized wherever Markdown prose is interpreted except inside an example body; never inside yaml, code, headings or table cells.
A machinery block whose x-grant is not 'default' is refused unless the operator granted that family. Grants are an independent set; refuse naming the family and the key to add.
An override may add tags, set disabled, or tighten an enum; it may not remove a tag, re-enable, widen an enum, replace a description, or change a default.
image digests are required (no mutable tags); a remote media/asset src requires sha256; runtime network=any is refused; a literal credential anywhere is refused.

A declared spec version this validator does not implement is a refusal. With unknown-sigiled this closes the silent path: a later version's machinery is either declared, and refused here, or sigiled and unknown, and refused there — never silently parsed as prose.
A document with no front matter, or with front matter lacking spec, is version 1.
